topic: Designing a GitHub Copilot multi-agent orchestrator — why five agents with every tool can turn one sentence into a green pull request that breaks on staging, and how least-privilege tools, send: false handoffs, hooks, CI gates and human sign-off put an owner back on the decision.

title.sub: Green checks are not an owner. Narrow tools, real gates, a named person.

stages.title: One sentence, five agents
stages.desc: You ask for a cancel reason. The agents run one after another, and none of them stops to ask you.
stages.status: Let customers give a reason when they cancel
stages.narration: One sentence starts five agents. None of them stops to ask you.

stages.title: No tools line means every tool
stages.desc: Leave out tools in an agent file and it defaults to all tools, including edit.
stages.narration: Leave out the tools line and the agent gets every tool.

stages.title: The tester edits production code
stages.desc: A test fails, so the tester widens canCancel in lib/ and the test goes green.
stages.narration: A test fails, so the tester changes production code until it goes green.

stages.title: The reviewer rewrites the rules
stages.desc: Asked to review, the security agent finds a real hole and edits firestore.rules itself.
stages.narration: Asked to review, the security agent rewrites the Firestore rules instead.

stages.title: Every check is green
stages.desc: CI passes because no test loads firestore.rules. The next day, cancel fails on staging.
stages.narration: CI is green, because no test loads the rules. Next day, cancel fails.

stages.title: Fix one: narrow the tools
stages.desc: Write a tools list for every agent. Security and the orchestrator lose edit completely.
stages.narration: Fix one. Write a tools list, so a reviewer simply cannot edit.

stages.title: Fix two: send false
stages.desc: A handoff with send: false pre-fills the next prompt and waits for you to read it.
stages.narration: Fix two. With send false, the next prompt waits for you.

stages.title: Fix three: real gates
stages.desc: A hook, required CI checks and CODEOWNERS block. Instructions and charters only ask.
stages.narration: Fix three. Hooks, required checks and code owners block. Charters only ask.

stages.title: Design the gates, own what ships
stages.desc: Agents do the work. A person owns what ships.
stages.narration: Design the gates. Own what ships.

end.title: Design the gates. Own what ships.
end.sub: Narrow tools, send: false, hooks and CI, then a person signs off by name.

post.caption:
One sentence. Five Copilot agents. A green pull request. And the next day, on staging, no customer can cancel an order. 🧭

Nothing crashed. Every agent made a reasonable local choice:

The tester widened production code to pass a test.
The security agent rewrote the rules instead of reporting.
CI stayed green because no test loads the rules.

The cause was in the agent files. No tools line means every tool.

Three fixes:

1. Write a tools list, so a reviewer cannot edit.
2. Use send: false, so a person reads each handoff.
3. Add hooks, required checks and CODEOWNERS, which block where instructions only ask.

Full guide: blog.msdevbuild.com/blog/github-copilot-multi-agent-orchestrator-legacy-teams

Follow for GitHub Copilot tips.
